question: Xi Jinping out before 2027?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if China's General Secretary of the Communist Party, Xi Jinping, is removed from power for any length of time between July 3, 2025, and December 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

CCP General Secretary Xi Jinping will be considered removed from power if he announces his resignation from his role as General Secretary, or is otherwise dismissed, detained, disqualified, or otherwise loses his position or is prevented from fulfilling his duties as General Secretary within this market's timeframe.

The primary resolution source for this market will be a consensus of credible reporting.

eventMetadata.context_description: Xi Jinping’s entrenched dominance over the Chinese Communist Party, Central Military Commission, and key state institutions underpins the near-certain trader consensus that he will remain in power through 2026. Recent high-level military purges have further aligned senior PLA ranks with his authority while removing potential rivals, and no formal retirement norms or designated successor apply to the paramount leader following the abolition of presidential term limits. The next scheduled leadership forum—the 21st Party Congress—lies in late 2027, with analyses pointing to expectations of continuity rather than abrupt change. While low-probability events such as a sudden health crisis, major undisclosed scandal, or unprecedented factional realignment could still intervene before year-end, no verifiable developments in the past several months indicate any near-term shift in his position.

question: Will Gavin Newsom win the 2028 Democratic presidential nomination?
description:

eventMetadata.context_description: Trader consensus positions Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez slightly ahead in the fragmented 2028 Democratic field, driven by her strength in early polling among younger and progressive voters alongside sustained media visibility. Jon Ossoff benefits from reelection momentum and perceived electability in battleground states, while Gavin Newsom draws on executive experience and fundraising but has seen his early lead narrow. Kamala Harris and Pete Buttigieg trail amid questions over past performance and positioning. With no primaries until 2028 and no dominant frontrunner above 21 percent, the tight distribution reflects ongoing party debates over ideology, generational change, and general-election viability. Future polling shifts, endorsements from key Senate and House leaders, and 2026 midterm results could widen gaps among the top contenders.
